w1.title: Worked Example 1: Moisture Content Reduction & Safe Water Activity
w1.question: A 15 kg batch of fresh mango slices loses 12 kg of water during solar drying. What is the dry yield weight?

steps.text: Given initial fresh weight = 15 kg and water evaporated = 12 kg.
Final dried mango yield = 3 kg (20% of fresh weight).

check.q: Why must warm humid air be continuously vented out of a solar dehydrator cabinet?

opts.t: So saturated air is replaced by dry warm air to keep evaporation going
To let rain enter the trays
opts.m: Vents are hooded against rain while exhausting humid air.
Stagnant humid air halts dehydration and causes mold.

w2.title: Worked Example 2: Temperature Control & Preventing Case Hardening
w2.question: What happens if drying temperature spikes above 80 °C on the first hour?

steps.text: Excessive surface heat rapidly forms a hard, dry crust on the fruit slice.
Internal moisture becomes trapped behind the sealed crust (case hardening).
Trapped internal moisture later causes spoilage during storage.

check.q: What is the ideal tray-loading practice for uniform airflow?

opts.t: Single layer of uniform-thickness slices with small gaps between pieces
Piling slices 10 cm deep in a heap
opts.m: Deep heaps block airflow and rot in the center.

opts.t: Mixing whole uncut fruits with thin slices
opts.m: Uniform slice thickness ensures all pieces finish drying together.

w3.title: Worked Example 3: Hygienic Packaging & Cooperative Unit Economics
w3.question: Why must dried slices cool to room temperature before sealing in pouches?

steps.text: Warm slices still release trace water vapor.
Sealing warm slices traps vapor that condenses into liquid droplets on the pouch wall.
Cooling in a clean dry chamber prevents condensation and mold.

check.q: If a cooperative spends ₹600 on fresh produce and sells 20 pouches at ₹45 each, what is the net surplus?

opts.m: ₹900 is total revenue (20 × 45); subtract the ₹600 cost to get ₹300.

steps.title: Moisture Content Reduction & Safe Water Activity
steps.body: Solar dehydration removes moisture from fresh produce (80–90% water) down to 10–15% so spoilage microbes cannot grow.

steps.title: Temperature Control & Preventing Case Hardening
steps.body: Maintaining cabinet temperature between 50 °C and 60 °C dries produce evenly without scorching vitamins or sealing the outer skin (case hardening).
